Proposes to have this discussed publicly, and will strive to defend it

units.la: Magnificentissimo, Prudentissimo & Con- sultissimo Viro, Domino DN. SAMUELI FRISCHINGIO, Illustris-Reipubl. Bernensis Consuli gravis- simo, Patriæ Patri optimo, Mœcenati suo clementissimo, ac susceptori è Sacro Ba- ptismatis fonte in æternum colendo.
units.tr: To the most magnificent, most prudent and most learned man, Lord Samuel Frisching, most grave consul of the Illustrious Republic of Bern, the best Father of the Fatherland, his most merciful patron, and the one to be revered forever as his sponsor at the sacred font of Baptism.

units.la: Reverendis item, Clarissimis, Doctissimisque VIRIS, D. D. Antistiti, Pastoribus, Diaconis, Professoribus Gymnasiarchæ, vigilantissimis, acutissimis, solertissimis, Ecclesiæ Scholæque Bernensis luminaribus, fautoribus, promotoribus & post DEUM patribus venerandis, suspiciendis.
units.tr: To the reverend, likewise the distinguished and most learned men, the Lord Antistes, the Pastors, the Deacons, the Professors, and the Rector of the Gymnasium, the most vigilant, most acute and most skilful luminaries of the Church and School of Bern, patrons, promoters, and, after God, venerable and esteemed fathers.

units.la: Hasce studiorum suorum Theologicorum primitias sacras merito esse vult
units.tr: He wishes these first fruits of his theological studies to be rightly dedicated to them.

units.la: DISPUTATIO TEXTUALIS. Theologica ex Joh. 3. v. 5. De REGENERATIONE.
units.tr: DISPUTATIO TEXTUALIS. Theological disputation on John 3:5, concerning REGENERATION.

units.la: Ἐὰν μὴ τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
units.tr: "Unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God." [Ἐὰν μὴ τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.]

units.la: ΕΝΟΣ δὲ χρεία[?]: sic respondit olim Christus Jesus Servator noster Marthæ, Luc. 10. v. 41. quæ suprà modum sollicita erat, & de multis satagebat, tacitè eam arguens τῆς πολυπραγμοσύνης[?], dùm ipsi non multa, sed unum ostendit, de quo debeat esse sollicita, nempè regnum cœlorum, unum necessarium, quo qui fruitur, omnia possidet, qui verò caret, omnibus caret: & quemadmodum regnum cælorum unum illud est, ad quod assequendum tendere debemus, ita unum est medium eò nos ducens, nempè Christus Jesus cum suis beneficiis, ex quorum primis est Regeneratio, de cujus necessitate ad regnum Dei consequendum Christus ipse Nicodemo concionatur, tùm in toto contextu, tùm in hoc ipso textu; cujus considerabimus occasionem, scopum & argumentum.
units.tr: "But one thing is needful" [ἑνὸς δὲ χρεία]: so once Christ Jesus our Saviour answered Martha, Luke 10:41, who was overly anxious and busied herself with many things, silently rebuking her for her busyness [τῆς πολυπραγμοσύνης], when he showed her not many things but one thing about which she ought to be concerned, namely the kingdom of heaven, the one necessary thing, which whoever enjoys possesses all things, but whoever lacks it lacks all things. And just as the kingdom of heaven is that one thing to which we ought to strive, so there is one means leading us to it, namely Christ Jesus with his benefits, the first of which is Regeneration. Christ himself preaches to Nicodemus about the necessity of this for attaining the kingdom of God, both throughout the whole context and in this very text. We shall consider its occasion, scope and argument.

units.la: Occasio erat Nicodemus, qui Christum noctu conveniebat, & ab illo doctrinam de regno coelorum seu salute obtinenda tanquam Prophetâ audire desiderabat, etsi enim quæstionem non expresse proponat, eam tamen fuisse illius mentem Christi responsio duplex ostendit; Nicodemus enim, cum responsionem primam à Christo datam male intelligeret ob metaphoricum sermonem, de modi potentia quæsivit, quam proinde Christus his verbis clarius exponit: Scopus itaq; est; Nicodemum erudire de necessitate & modo Regenerationis nostræ.
units.tr: The occasion was Nicodemus, who came to Christ by night and desired to hear from him, as from a prophet, the teaching about the kingdom of heaven, or about obtaining salvation. For although he does not expressly put the question, Christ's twofold answer shows that this was his mind. Nicodemus, since he misunderstood the first answer given by Christ because of its metaphorical language, asked about the manner of the power, which Christ therefore explains more clearly in these words. The scope, then, is: to instruct Nicodemus about the necessity and manner of our Regeneration.

units.la: Argumentum ergo loci clarum est; partes duæ, extrema & eorundem necessaria connexio; Extremorum unum continet medium, alterum vero finem.
units.tr: The argument of the passage is therefore clear. There are two parts: the extremes and the necessary connection between them. One of the extremes contains the means, the other the end.

units.la: Medium tum repetitur ex v. 3. γεννηθῇ [?], tum declaratur à causa efficiente, simul includente modum generationis illius, appositè ad interrogationem Nicodemi, ἐξ ὕδατος [?] καὶ πνεύματος.
units.tr: The means is both repeated from v. 3, γεννηθῇ [gennēthē, "is born"], and described by its efficient cause, which at the same time includes the manner of that generation, aptly answering Nicodemus's question: ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος [ex hydatos kai pneumatos, "of water and Spirit"].

units.la: Generatio ergo hic nō intelligitur carnalis sive naturalis, quomodo Christus genitus dicitur ex Maria Virgine, Matth. 1. v. 16. Luc. 1. v. 35. & qualem Nicodemus sibi imaginatus esse videtur; sed spiritualis, de qua, 1. Pet. 2. v. 2. quæ alias vocatur circumcisio cordis non manu facta, creatio, renovatio Spiritus S. γέννησις ἄνωθεν, regeneratio.
units.tr: Therefore generation here is not understood as carnal or natural, the way Christ is said to be begotten of the Virgin Mary, Matt. 1:16; Luke 1:35, and in the way Nicodemus seems to have imagined it. It is spiritual, of which 1 Pet. 2:2 speaks; it is also called the circumcision of the heart not made by hand, creation, renewal of the Holy Spirit, γέννησις ἄνωθεν [gennēsis anōthen, "birth from above"], regeneration.

units.la: Hinc hoc modo geniti dicuntur regeniti non ex semine corruptibili, sed incorruptibili, id est, per sermonem Dei vivi & manentis in æternum, 1. Pet. 1. v. 23. geniti in Christo Iesu per Evangelium, 1. Joh. 5. v. 1. geniti vel nati ex Deo. Joh. 1. v. 13.
units.tr: In this way those who are begotten are called regenerate: not from corruptible seed but incorruptible, that is, through the word of the living God which abides forever, 1 Pet. 1:23; begotten in Christ Jesus through the Gospel, 1 John 5:1; begotten or born of God, John 1:13.

units.la: Efficiens Regenerationis est spiritus, qui hic per hendyadyn vocatur aqua & spiritus, nec enim diversas Regenerationis causas hic significari autumamus; principalem nempe τὸ πνεῦμα, & instrumentalem τὸ ὕδωρ aquam, quam proprie dictam & κατ' ἐξοχὴν illam baptismi quidam intelligi volunt. 1. quia interpretatio per hendyadyn analoga est tum contextui, qui agit de conditione sive medio absolute necessario consequendæ salutis, qualis non est baptismus; & verò v. 6. 8. solius Spiritus meminit; tum S. Scripturæ, quæ alibi etiam aquam & spiritum pro eodem sumit. Esai. 44. v. 3. Ezech. 36. v. 25. 26. 27.
units.tr: The efficient cause of Regeneration is the Spirit, which here is called by hendiadys water and Spirit. For we do not think that two different causes of Regeneration are meant here, the principal one, namely τὸ πνεῦμα [to pneuma, "the Spirit"], and the instrumental one, τὸ ὕδωρ [to hydōr, "the water"], which some wish to understand as water properly so called and κατ' ἐξοχήν [kat' exochēn, "pre-eminently"], that of baptism. First, because the interpretation by hendiadys is consistent both with the context, which treats of a condition or means of obtaining salvation that is absolutely necessary, which baptism is not, and indeed in v. 6 and 8 it mentions only the Spirit; and with Holy Scripture, which elsewhere also takes water and Spirit for the same thing: Isa. 44:3; Ezek. 36:25, 26, 27.

units.la: 2. Aqua hæc certò Regenerat, & aptum hominem reddit ad subeundum regnum cœlorum, ut patet ex textu; non item aqua baptismi, ut patet exemplo Simonis Magi, Act. 8. v. 13.
units.tr: 2. This water certainly regenerates and makes a man fit to enter the kingdom of heaven, as is evident from the text. The water of baptism does not do so, as is evident from the example of Simon Magus, Acts 8:13.

units.la: Genitum igitur esse ex aqua & Spiritu est à Spiritu S. vim aquæ exerente purgatum, mundatum & renovatum esse: præstat enim in Regeneratione animæ Spiritus Sanctus, quod aqua corpori in lotione: non ex operibus justis, quæ fecerimus nos; sed ex sua misericordia servavit nos per lavacrum Regenerationis, Renovationis Spiritus Sancti, Tit. 3. v. 5. Similis loquendi forma occurrit, Matth. 3. v. 10, 11. is baptizabit vos Spiritu Sancto & igne.
units.tr: To be begotten of water and Spirit therefore means to be cleansed, purified and renewed, the power of the water being exercised by the Holy Spirit. For the Holy Spirit accomplishes in the soul in regeneration what water does for the body in washing: "not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit", Titus 3:5. A similar form of speech occurs in Matt. 3:10, 11: "he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire."

units.la: Finis est possessio regni cœlorum, εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, & ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, v. 3. nihil aliud est, quàm habere vitam æternam, v. 15. 16. possidere hæreditario jure regnum paratum à jacto mundi fundamento, Matth. 25. v. 34. quamvis sint qui existiment Christum plus dicere in textu, quàm in v. 3. quum plus sit introire regnum cœlorum, quàm illud tantùm videre; cùm ergò Christus dicat, non potest videre regnum Dei, notari Regenerationis necessitatem tantam, ut sine illa necquidem possimus videre regnum coelorum, nedum possidere. Quando autem in textu dicat non posse introire, notari Regenerationis maximum privilegium, quòd regeniti non tantùm regnum Dei videant, sed etiam possideant.
units.tr: The end is possession of the kingdom of heaven, εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ [eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou theou, "to enter the kingdom of God"], and ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ [idein tēn basileian tou theou, "to see the kingdom of God"], v. 3. This is nothing other than having eternal life, vv. 15, 16, possessing by hereditary right the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world, Matt. 25:34. Some think that Christ says more in the text than in v. 3, since entering the kingdom of heaven is more than merely seeing it. Yet since Christ says, he cannot see the kingdom of God, it is noted that the necessity of Regeneration is so great that without it we cannot even see the kingdom of heaven, much less possess it. But when in the text he says that one cannot enter, it is noted that Regeneration has the greatest privilege: the regenerate not only see the kingdom of God but also possess it.

units.la: Per regnum Dei hic non intelligitur illud potentia, de quo 1. Chron. 29. v.11[?]. Tuum Jehovah est regnum, quod etiam universale & οἰκουμενικὸν, itemque essentiale dicitur; nec regnum gratiae, licet enim Regeneratio sit introitus in hoc regnum, de eo tamen hic non quaeritur, ut patet ex circumstantiis, verum regnum Gloriae, quod etiam regnum coelorum hinc inde in Sacra Scriptura dicitur.
units.tr: By the kingdom of God is not meant here that kingdom of power of which 1 Chron. 29:11 says, "Thine, O Jehovah, is the kingdom", which is also called universal, οἰκουμενικός [oikoumenikos, "of the world"], and likewise essential. Nor is it the kingdom of grace: although Regeneration is the entrance into this kingdom, this is not the subject here, as is clear from the circumstances. It is rather the kingdom of glory, which in Holy Scripture is also called the kingdom of heaven in various places.

units.la: Connexio extremorum notatur particulis ἐὰν μή, ἢ δύνα-ται, quibus necessarius inter eadem nexus significatur; ut nulli detur introitus in regnum coelorum, nisi genito ex aqua & Spiritu: ut sic Regeneratio ad consequendum regnum Dei se habeat ut necessarium medium & requisitum ad finem hominis.
units.tr: The connection of the extremes is marked by the particles ἐὰν μή [ean mē, "unless"] and οὐ δύναται [ou dynatai, "cannot"], by which a necessary bond between them is signified: that no one has entrance into the kingdom of heaven unless he is born of water and Spirit. Thus Regeneration stands to attaining the kingdom of God as the necessary means and the requirement for man's end.

units.la: Doctrina, quae ex hoc textu efflorescit, haec est, quòd unicuiq; in Adamo mortuo Regeneratio ex aqua & Spiritu tàm sit necessaria, ut sine ea regnum Dei introire nequeat: quam ut eò felicius elaboremus consideraraimus[?] 1. Ipsam Regenerationis naturam. 2. Ejus necessitatem.
units.tr: The doctrine that flows from this text is this: that Regeneration by water and Spirit is so necessary for every person who is dead in Adam that without it he cannot enter the kingdom of God. That we may work this out more fruitfully, let us consider 1. the very nature of Regeneration; 2. its necessity.

units.la: Natura Regenerationis ex descriptione ejus innotescit, quae talis est: Regeneratio est beneficium Dei ex multa Patris misericordia in Christo nobis collatum, quo homini in Adamo spiritualiter mortuo, attamen electo & per Christum redempto vita vita spiritualis de novo inditur, ad gloriosæ Dei misericordiæ demonstrationem & hominis salutem.
units.tr: The nature of Regeneration is made known from its description, which is as follows: Regeneration is a benefit of God, bestowed upon us in Christ from the great mercy of the Father, by which life is again breathed spiritually into a man who is spiritually dead in Adam, yet elect and redeemed through Christ, to the demonstration of the glorious mercy of God and the salvation of man.

units.la: Regenerationem Paulus nominat παλιγγενεσίαν [?], Tit.3.v.5. Præpositio insepatabilis re videtur notare aliquam iteratam generationem, ita ut Regeneratio vi Etymologiæ sit quasi altera vel secunda generatio; quæ ita dicitur, non quòd aliqua similis generatio præcesserit, quæ ceu imperfecta secundâ aliquâ generatione perficienda sit, sed respectu generationis carnalis sive naturalis; à qua quidem tota specie differt, interim tamen propter analogiam quæ inter utramque est, ita dicitur..
units.tr: Paul names Regeneration παλιγγενεσία [palingenesia, "regeneration"], Titus 3:5. The inseparable prefix re- seems to signify some repeated generation, so that by the etymology regeneration is, as it were, a second or another generation. It is so called not because some similar generation preceded it, which, being imperfect, was to be completed by a second generation, but with respect to carnal or natural generation. From this it differs entirely in kind, yet it is called so because of the analogy that exists between the two.

units.la: Analogia illa in multis ostendi potest; in termino à quo: Generatio naturalis est à non esse ad esse; ita & Regenera-tio: in causa efficiente; generatio naturalis perficitur à Patre & matre, sic Regeneratio est à Patre 1.Pet.1,v.3. & à vel in Matre Ecclesia: Illa est è semine carnali; Joh. 1: 13. hæc est è semine ἀφθάρτῳ [?] 1, Pet. 1: 23. Illius terminus ad quem est homo naturalis; hujus verò novus suis constans membris: Illa est ad vitam naturalem; hæc ad spiritualem: Illâ conservatur species humana; hâc verò Ecclesia: Illa fit semel tantùm; ita & hæc.
units.tr: This analogy can be shown in many respects. In the terminus from which: natural generation is from non-being to being; so too Regeneration. In the efficient cause: natural generation is brought about by a father and mother; so Regeneration is from the Father, 1 Pet. 1:3, and from or in the mother, the Church. The former is from carnal seed, John 1:13; the latter is from incorruptible seed, 1 Pet. 1:23. The terminus to which of the former is natural man; of the latter, a new man made up of its own members. The former is to natural life; the latter to spiritual life. By the former the human species is preserved; by the latter, the Church. The former happens only once; so too the latter.

units.la: Regenerationis vox vulgò sumitur duplici modo vel pro illo instanti, quo per incorruptibile semen verbi divini renascimur ex Dei spiritu, & simus nova Creatura; vel pro successivo illo, quo per Spiritum Regenerationis, quicquid est carnis in nobis paulatim atteritur: ut deposito quoad pristinam conversationem attinet veteri illo homine, qui de seductricibus cupiditatibus sese corrumpit, renovemur spiritu mentis nostræ, & induamus novum illum hominem qui secundùm Deum conditus est ad justitiam & sanctimoniam veram Eph.4.v.22.23. Priori modo si sumatur, Regeneratio coincidit cum donatione fidei & resipiscentiae, seu prima conversione, quomodo à sanctificatione distinguitur: si vero posteriori modo sumatur pro ea nempe Regeneratione, ubi quis incipit secundum Regenerationem suam vivere, ita ut habitus incipiat crescere ipso exercitio pietatis, ab ipsa sanctificatione non alia est.
units.tr: The word regeneration is commonly used in two senses: either for that instant in which we are born again through the incorruptible seed of the divine word, by the Spirit of God, and become a new creature; or for that gradual process by which, through the Spirit of regeneration, whatever is of the flesh in us is worn away little by little, so that, as far as our former conduct goes, we put off the old man, who corrupts himself through deceitful desires, are renewed in the spirit of our mind, and put on the new man, who has been created according to God in true righteousness and holiness, Eph. 4:22-23. If it is taken in the first sense, regeneration coincides with the gift of faith and repentance, or first conversion, and in this sense it is distinguished from sanctification. But if it is taken in the second sense, namely for that regeneration in which someone begins to live according to his regeneration, so that the habit begins to grow by the very exercise of piety, then it is not other than sanctification itself.

units.la: Quando generis loco in definitione ponimus beneficium, loquimur cum Apostolo 1. Pet.1. v.3. Benedictus Deus & Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi qui ex multa sua misericordia regenuit nos in spem vivam.
units.tr: When we put benefit in the definition in place of the genus, we speak with the Apostle, 1 Pet. 1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has begotten us again to a living hope.

units.la: Causa efficiens principalis Regenerationis est Deus, qui nos regenerat, & hinc dicimur filij Dei, qui non ex sanguine, neq; ex libidine carnis, neq; ex libidine viri, sed ex Deo geniti sunt. Regeneratio, quia est opus Dei ad extra, propterea unicuique in Sacro Sancta Trinitate adscribitur, Sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, sed justificati estis in nomine Domini Jesu & per Spiritum Dei nostri, 1.Cor.6.v.11. Quemadmodum enim in Divinitate unica saltem est essentia, & tamen unius ejusdemque essentiae tres distinctae personae, sic quoque in operibus Dei externis omnes tres personae ad unum idemque opus concurrunt & cooperantur, verum non uno eodemq; modo, exempli gratia; opera creationis, redemptionis & sanctificationis sunt opera communia Patri, Filio & Spiritui Sancto, & quodlibet horum operum omnibus tribus commune ipsis in specie adscribitur. Ergo regeneratio-nis causa est tota S.S. Trinitas, singulariter autem Spiritus Sanctus, & eo respicit Christus in textu: Nisi quis genitus sit ex aqua & Spiritu: ideò ab hoc potissimum effectu Spiritus Dei Sanctus & Sanctificationis sæpe dicitur.
units.tr: The principal efficient cause of regeneration is God, who regenerates us, and hence we are called children of God, who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. Because regeneration is a work of God outward, it is therefore ascribed to each person of the Most Holy Trinity: But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God, 1 Cor. 6:11. For just as in the one Divinity there is only one essence, and yet three distinct persons of the one and the same essence, so too in the external works of God all three persons come together and cooperate in one and the same work, yet not in one and the same way. For example, the works of creation, redemption and sanctification are common works of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and each of these works, though common to all three, is nonetheless ascribed to each in particular. Therefore the cause of regeneration is the whole Holy Trinity, but in particular the Holy Spirit, and it is to this that Christ refers in the text: Unless someone is born of water and the Spirit. Hence the Spirit of God is often called Holy and Sanctifier chiefly from this effect.

units.la: Errant igitur Sociniani, qui Spiritum Sanctum non nisi regenitis & jam sanctificatis dari nugantur, nam hoc modo authorem Regenerationis eum esse negant: cùm Regenerationis opus vel eo nomine rectè ei tribuatur, quòd à Patre & Filio procedat per spirationem, cujus proinde est suo flatu nos purgare & purificare, quod est ipsum opus Regenerationis sive Sanctificationis.
units.tr: The Socinians therefore err, who trifle that the Holy Spirit is given only to the regenerate and those already sanctified; for in this way they deny that he is the author of regeneration. Yet the work of regeneration is rightly ascribed to him, if for no other reason than that he proceeds from the Father and the Son by breathing, and it is therefore his to cleanse and purify us by his breath, which is the very work of regeneration or sanctification.

units.la: Spiritus Sanctus, cùm sit causa Regenerationis, regenerat nos efficaci sua præsentia & potentia, nam ut quotquot Spiritu Dei aguntur, ij sunt filij Dei, Rom. 8. v.14. Ita eo agi convenit, quotquot filii Dei revera sunt; uti Patris amorem non nisi per filium consequimur, ita filij beneficiorum per solum Spiritum sanctificationis fimus participes; imò per hoc cognoscimus nos in eo habitare & ipsum in nobis, quod de Spiritu suo dedit nobis, 1. Joh. 4. v. 13.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit, since he is the cause of regeneration, regenerates us by his effective presence and power: for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God, Rom. 8:14. It is fitting that all who are truly sons of God are led by him, just as we obtain the Father's love only through the Son, so the sons become partakers of the benefits only through the Spirit of sanctification. Indeed, by this we know that we dwell in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit, 1 John 4:13.

units.la: Sunt autè certa τεκμήρια ex Verbo Dei desumpta, per quæ quivis fideles certò possunt scire, quòd in ipsis sit, imprimis quando cum Verbo Dei convenientes motus & operationes in se sentiunt, certò concludere licet, se habere Spiritum Sanctum; qui itaque ex Pontificijs nos judicant superbos vel melancholicos, quòd de præsentia & efficacia Spiritus Sancti in cordibus nostris gloriemur, illi nesciunt, quid sit esse Filium Dei & Christianum.
units.tr: There are certain signs (τεκμήρια) drawn from the Word of God, by which any faithful person can be certain that he has the Spirit within him. Above all, when he feels in himself motions and operations that agree with the Word of God, he may rightly conclude that he has the Holy Spirit. Those Papists, therefore, who judge us proud or melancholic because we glory in the presence and efficacy of the Holy Spirit in our hearts, do not know what it is to be a son of God and a Christian.

units.la: Est autem illa potentia, quâ Spiritus Sanctus utitur in natura hominis restauranda & reparanda tantæ virtutis, ut insuperabiliter rem det effectam, quod probat Spiritus Sanctus locis, Ezech. 36.v.26.27. Et dabo vobis cor novum & Spiritum novum ponam in medio vestri, & auferam cor lapideum è carne vestra, indam vobis cor carneum: & spiritum meum ponam in medio vestri; quo faciam ut in Statutis meis ambuletis, & jura mea observetis, facientes ea. Jerem.32. v.39. Indam enim illis cor unum & viam unam, ad reverendum me omnibus diebus, ad bonum ipsorum & filiorum ipsorum post ipsos. Phil.2:13. Deus enim is est, qui in vobis efficit & ipsum velle & ipsum agere pro gratuita benevolentia.
units.tr: Now that power which the Holy Spirit uses in restoring and repairing human nature is of such virtue that he brings the matter to its effect unconquerably. The Spirit proves this in places such as Ezek. 36:26-27: And I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit in the midst of you, and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh, and I will put my Spirit in the midst of you, so that you may walk in my statutes and observe my judgments, doing them. Jer. 32:39: And I will give them one heart and one way, to fear me all their days, for their good and the good of their children after them. Phil. 2:13: For it is God who works in you both to will and to do, for his gracious goodwill.

units.la: Huc & illud spectat, quod Apostolus hujus [?]ἐνεργείας virtutem tàm magnificè effert, ut sibi satisfacere quasi nequeat: Vocat enim eam non modò δύναμιν, sed & μεγέθος δυνάμεως, neque id solùm, sed & ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος τῆς δυνάμεως τῆς [?]κράτους τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτῆς, Eph.1.v.19. Quæ nemo, cui non periit frons, negare potest, significare vim, potentiam & efficaciam, qua frangitur & prosternitur voluntatis humanæ superbia & contumacia naturæ adversùs Deum in ordinem cogitur: quæ verò adversarii non unius generis objiciunt ex Sacra Scriptura, ea videbimus in ipso disputationis actu.
units.tr: To this also refers the fact that the Apostle sets forth the power of this energy [ἐνεργείας] so magnificently that he seems unable to satisfy himself. For he calls it not only power [δύναμιν], but the greatness of power [μεγέθος δυνάμεως], and not only that, but the surpassing greatness of his power [ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος τῆς δυνάμεως], according to the working of the might of his strength [κράτους τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτῆς], Eph. 1:19. No one who is not shameless can deny that these words signify a force, power and efficacy by which the pride of the human will is broken and cast down, and the obstinacy of nature against God is brought into order. Whatever objections our adversaries bring from Holy Scripture of no single kind, we shall see in the very course of the disputation.

units.la: Cur autem Spiritus Sanctus Regenerationis donum quibusdam conferat, quibusdam verò non, & quid Spiritum Sanctum ad hunc vel illum regenerandum moveat, præter [?]εὐδοκίαν Dei in hominibus nullam videmus causam: nec enim causa esse possunt dispositiones previæ aut præparatio per quandam docilitatem & animi probitatem, aut melior nostri naturalis arbitrij usus ante actualem conversionem; uti adversarij perperam sentiunt; nam postquàm benignitas & erga homines amor apparuit Servatoris nostri Dei,non ex operibus justis, quæ fecerimus nos, sed ex sua misericordia servavit nos per lavacrum Regenerationis, renovationis Spiritus Sancti, quem effudit super nos copiosè per Jesum Christum Servatorem nostrum, Tit.3. v.4. s.6. praeter εὐδοκίαν[?] Dei causa [illegible, ~12 letters] sive meritoria extra nos est meritum Jesu Christi, propter quod Deus donat nos Spiritu Sancto & restituit in nobis imaginem suam.
units.tr: Why the Holy Spirit bestows the gift of regeneration on some but not on others, and what moves the Spirit to regenerate this or that person, we see no cause except the good pleasure [εὐδοκίαν] of God toward men. Nor can previous dispositions or preparation through a certain docility and uprightness of mind, or a better use of our natural free will before actual conversion, be the cause, as our adversaries wrongly think. For after the kindness and love toward men of our Saviour God appeared, he saved us not by works of righteousness which we had done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour, Titus 3:4-6. Apart from the good pleasure of God, the cause outside us, or the meritorious cause, is the merit of Jesus Christ, on account of which God gives us the Holy Spirit and restores his image in us. [illegible]

units.la: Qui enim adulti primùm regenerantur, in iis quidem accedere, imò & praecedere solet verbum externum, tanquàm causa instrumentalis moralis; cujus tamen salutaris efficacia pendet ab interna reali operatione Sp.Sancti, sed infantium electorum & in foedere natorum communiter alia est ratio; ubi res verbi à parentibus fide recepti, quantum ad principium intus menti inditur per Spiritum regenerantem; unde ea postmodùm, accedente etiam verbo externo ad actus secundos promovetur: In adultis regenerandis verbum est tùm Legis tùm Evangelij; illud se habet instar mallei, quò cor lapideum confringitur; instar ignis, quò cor induratum fit molle & colliquescit; instar gladij, qui penetrat & pertingit usq; ad divisionem animae simul ac spiritus, compagumq; & medullarum, & dijudicat cogitationes & conceptus cordis, Heb.4. v.12. Hoc autem se habet instar olei, quò cor fractum, liquefactum & vulneratum emollitur & vulnera cordis sanantur, & cor infirmum & trepidum confortatur & restituitur promissionibus Dei in Christo propositis. Per legem tàm naturae inscriptam, Rom.1. quàm lapideis tabulis renovatam, 1.Cor.3. homo ad veram miseriae suae agnitionem perducitur: Per Evangelium verò & promissiones ejus, dolor secundum Deum concipitur, conscientia afflicta in spem veniae erigitur, Christus denique apprehenditur, non tantùm in remissionem peccatorum, sed abolitionem quoque Veteris & resuscitationem novi hominis; Unde & Evangelium ministerium Spiritus & vitæ appellatur, 2. Cor. 3.
units.tr: Those who are regenerated first as adults are usually helped, and indeed preceded, by the external word, as a moral instrumental cause. Yet its saving efficacy depends on the inner real operation of the Holy Spirit. But for elect infants and those born within the covenant, the case is generally different: the thing of the word, received in faith by the parents, is placed inwardly in the mind by the regenerating Spirit; from there it is afterwards advanced to second acts, the external word also being added. In adults to be regenerated the word is both of the Law and of the Gospel. As a hammer, it breaks the stony heart; as a fire, it makes the hardened heart soft and melts it; as a sword, it penetrates and reaches even to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart, Heb. 4:12. It also acts as oil, by which the broken, melted and wounded heart is softened, the wounds of the heart are healed, and the weak and trembling heart is strengthened and restored by the promises of God set forth in Christ. Through the law, written in nature (Rom. 1) and renewed on the stone tablets (1 Cor. 3), a man is brought to a true knowledge of his misery. But through the Gospel and its promises, sorrow according to God is conceived, the afflicted conscience is raised up to hope of pardon, and Christ is at last laid hold of, not only for the forgiveness of sins but also for the abolition of the old man and the resurrection of the new man. Hence the Gospel is also called the ministry of the Spirit and of life, 2 Cor. 3.

units.la: Materia in qua vel subjectum, & materia circa quam sive objectum Regenerationis, non est Angelus: neque bonus, quia Regeneratione non eget; neque malus, quia istius gratiæ non potest fieri particeps; neque irrationalis creatura, aut substantia merè materialis, quia ejus non est capax; sed est homo, & spiritualiter quidem mortuus in Adamo, alienatus à vitâ Dei, Eph. 2. v. 1. s. & 4. 18. atque adeò ea egens, ut salvetur, & gratia Dei salutifera in ipso efficaciter demonstretur: Sed electus in Christo: Deus enim omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suæ, Eph. 1. imò & redemptus per Christū,Christus enim electis suis istam vitam impetravit, & juxta impetrationem ea producitur.
units.tr: The matter in which, or subject of, Regeneration, and the matter about which, or object of, Regeneration, is not an angel: not a good one, because he does not need regeneration; nor an evil one, because he cannot become a partaker of this grace; nor an irrational creature, or a purely material substance, because it is not capable of it. It is man, who is spiritually dead in Adam, alienated from the life of God, Eph. 2:1 ff. and 4:18, and therefore needs it in order to be saved, and in whom the saving grace of God is effectively displayed. He is chosen in Christ: for God works all things according to the counsel of his will, Eph. 1. Indeed he is also redeemed through Christ, for Christ obtained this life for his chosen ones, and it is brought forth in accordance with that obtaining.

units.la: [?]liquè non tantùm adulti, sed etiam infantes, qui sicut servantur, ita etiam regenerari & sanctificari necesse est I. Quia nemo electorum ad vitam æternam è præsenti vita evocatur, qui non prius regeneretur & sanctificetur Dei spiritu: nam caro & sanguis regnum Dei possidere non potest: in regnum Dei nihil ingreditur pollutum aut coinquinatum: nullis patet in vitam cœlestem ingressus nisi renatis, Joh. 3. v. 3. II. Quia ideò à primâ infantiâ sanctificatus fuit Christus, ut ex ætate qualibet sine discrimine electos suos in seipso sanctificaret. III. Quia Jeremias Propheta & Johannes Baptista in materno utero sanctificati dicuntur; Jerem. 1. v. 5. ait Deus ad Jeremiam: quùm nondum prodiisses ex vulva, sanctificavi te Luc. 1. v. 17. ait Angelus de Johanne Baptista: Spiritu Sancto implebitur etiam à ventre matris suæ: In his infantibus documentum Deus præbuit, buïr, quid in reliquis possit, imò quid in reliquis revera etiam præstet, etsi à nobis non ita observetur semper.
units.tr: Clearly it is necessary that not only adults but also infants be regenerated and sanctified by the Spirit of God, just as they are saved. (1) Because no one of the elect is called out of this present life to eternal life who is not first regenerated and sanctified by the Spirit of God: for flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God; nothing defiled or polluted enters into the kingdom of God; there is no entrance into heavenly life except for the reborn, Joh. 3:3. (2) Because for this reason Christ was sanctified from earliest infancy, so that he might sanctify his elect in himself at every age without distinction. (3) Because the prophet Jeremiah and John the Baptist are said to have been sanctified in the mother's womb. Jer. 1:5: God says to Jeremiah, before you came forth from the womb I sanctified you; Luke 1:17: the angel says of John the Baptist, he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb. In these infants God has given a proof of what he can do in the rest, indeed of what in fact he also accomplishes in the rest, although we do not always observe it in this way.

units.la: Sicut autem principale peccati subjectum est anima hominis, omnibus suis naturalibus facultatibus instructa, corpus verò minus principale, tanquàm animæ sedes & instrumentum; ita & Regenerationis propria sedes & subjectum principale eadem anima secundùm omnes facultates suas, intellectum, voluntatem & affectus: Intellectus ante Regenerationem est obtenebratus, veraque & salutari Dei notitia orbatus, 1. Cor. 2. v. 14. per Regenerationem irradiatur & illuminatur: Hinc David petit, Psal. 119. mentis oculos sibi aperiri ad videnda mirabilia legis divinæ. Voluntas hominis ante Regenerationè dislorta & ab obsequio Dei aliena, Jerem. 13. v. 23. An mutare potest Æthiops cutem suam, aut pardus liventes maculas suas? etiam vos possetis benefacere, edocti malefacere, Rom. 3. v. 12. Non est qui faciat bonum, non est usquè ad unum; per Regenerationem emollitur & ad obsequium flectitur, Jerem. 32. v. 8. Reverentiam mei indam animo illorum, ut non recedant à me, Ezech. 11. v. 20. Quod observatum volumus contra Socinianos, qui voluntatem Regenerationis inhærente gratia affici negare audent. Assectus hominis, quales sunt amor, ira, æmulatio, desiderium, odium, lætitia, tristitia &c. ante Regenerationem sunt effrænati; per Regenerationem intemperies paulatim sanatur, ut in rectæ & per Spiritum renovatæ rationis gyrum se contrahi patiantur: Huc pertinet illud Pauli, Gal. 5. v. 24. qui suam carnem crucifixerunt cum affectibus & cupiditatibus.
units.tr: Just as the principal subject of sin is the soul of man, furnished with all its natural faculties, while the body is less principal, as the seat and instrument of the soul, so too the proper seat and principal subject of Regeneration is the same soul, according to all its faculties: the intellect, the will and the affections. The intellect, before Regeneration, is darkened and deprived of the true and saving knowledge of God, 1 Cor. 2:14; through Regeneration it is illuminated and enlightened. Hence David asks that the eyes of his mind be opened to see the wonders of the divine law, Ps. 119. The will of man before Regeneration is perverted and alien to the obedience of God: Jer. 13:23, Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Then may you also do good, who are taught to do evil; Rom. 3:12, There is none who does good, no, not one. Through Regeneration it is softened and bent to obedience, Jer. 32:8, I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they do not depart from me; Ezek. 11:20. We wish this to be noted against the Socinians, who dare to deny that the will of the regenerate is affected by inherent grace. The affections of man, such as love, anger, emulation, desire, hatred, joy, sorrow, etc., before Regeneration are unbridled; through Regeneration their disorder is gradually healed, so that they allow themselves to be drawn into the orbit of right reason renewed through the Spirit. To this belongs that saying of Paul, Gal. 5:24, those who have crucified their flesh with its affections and lusts.

units.la: Forma Regenerationis consistit in reali mutatione hominis, per impressionem sive inditionem novæ vitæ, qua homo fit nova creatura; quæ inde vivificatio novi hominis dicitur. Sicut autem unius generatio est alterius corruptio; ita hic vivificationem novi hominis sequitur mortificatio Veteris; quæ in corruptionis & pravitatis nostræ nativæ abolitione, suis gradibus constante, de quibus Catechismus, consistit.
units.tr: The form of Regeneration consists in a real change of the man, through the impression or infusion of a new life, by which the man becomes a new creature; this is called the vivification of the new man. But just as the generation of one thing is the corruption of another, so the vivification of the new man is followed here by the mortification of the Old, which consists in the abolition of our native corruption and depravity, proceeding by its stages, of which the Catechism speaks.

units.la: Non itaq; consistit Regeneratio in actionum tantum & vitæ anteactæ mutatione, verum in ipsius naturæ interna reali & hyperphysica mutatione; qua Veteris hominis natura non tantum reprimitur, moresq; mutantur, sed etiam aboletur, & vera sanctitas ac justitia ejus loco substituitur, quod observandum est contra Socinianos, qui eam tantum in anteactæ vitæ mutatione, atq; ad Christi legem conformatione ponunt: quia videlicet corruptionem naturæ non agnoscunt, unde etiam adultis solum Regenerationem competere existimant, contra Scripturæ Authoritatem, quæ prout naturæ nostræ scaturiginem vitiatam, ac sontem ipsum insincerum esse docet, ita universum hominem, mentem, voluntatem, affectus, corpus ac membra deniq; omnia regenerari debere docet; nec adultos solum, sed ipsos quoq; infantes beneficij istius participes facit. 1.Thessal. 5: 23. Ipse vero Deus pacis sanctificet vos [?]ὁλοτελεῖς, integros, Eph. 4: 23. Renovari autem spiritu mentis vestræ. Gen. 8. v. 21. Eo quod figmentum cordis hominis sit malum à pueritia ipsius. Rom. 7. v. 14. & 6. v. 12. 19. Luc. 1. v. 15. & v. 80.
units.tr: Regeneration therefore does not consist merely in a change of actions and of the former life, but in a real and hyperphysical change of the inner nature itself, by which the nature of the Old Man is not only restrained and his manners changed, but is also abolished, and true holiness and righteousness are substituted in its place. This must be noted against the Socinians, who locate it only in a change of the former life and in conformity to the law of Christ. They do so because they do not acknowledge the corruption of nature, whence they also think that Regeneration belongs only to adults, against the authority of Scripture, which teaches that the spring of our nature is vitiated and the source itself is unsound; so it teaches that the whole man, mind, will, affections, body and members, must finally all be regenerated, and it makes not only adults but infants also partakers of this benefit. 1 Thess. 5:23, And may the God of peace himself sanctify you wholly [ὁλοτελεῖς], entire; Eph. 4:23, and be renewed in the spirit of your mind; Gen. 8:21, because the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth; Rom. 7:14, and 6:12, 19; Luke 1:15 and 1:80.

units.la: Respectu horum actuum formalium idea & exemplar perfectissimum est Christus crucifixus, mortuus, & è mortuis suscitatus, cum quo nos unà crucifigi & resurgere decet, Matth. 11. v. 29. Huic coalescimus assimilatione mortis, atq; etiam resurrectionis ipsius Rom. 6. v. 4. s. Christus enim morte sua beneficium istud nobis acquisivit: atque ut moriens, mortificationis illius, sic resurgens vivificationis quodammodo causa exemplaris, & simul virtualiter causa efficiens principalis existit.
units.tr: With respect to these formal acts, the idea and most perfect pattern is Christ crucified, dead, and raised from the dead, with whom it is fitting for us to be crucified and to rise together, Matt. 11:29. We are joined to him by conformity to his death and also to his resurrection itself, Rom. 6:4 ff. For Christ acquired this benefit for us by his death; and as dying he is the cause of that mortification, so rising he is in some sense the exemplary cause of vivification, and at the same time, virtually, the principal efficient cause.

units.la: Modus Regenerationis, quo Spiritus Sanctus utitur in regenerandis hominibus, pro diversis subjectis diversimodè se habet, aliter se habet in adultis, qui plerunque valdè est sensibilis, dum nova ista luce perculsus animus stupet, ac ad proprias sordes horret & æstuat, nec sine motu Spiritus Sancti opus suum peragit. Hoc audito compuncti sunt corde, Act. 2. v. 37. Aliter in infantibus in Ecclesia natis, interque faustas sanctorum preces in sinu ejus educatis se res habet. A teneris Deo dedicati magis regenitos sese[?] esse deprehendunt, quàm regenerari senserunt, fere ut in naturali generatione videmus.
units.tr: The mode of Regeneration, which the Holy Spirit uses in regenerating men, varies according to the different subjects. It is one way in adults, in whom it is for the most part very perceptible, while the mind, struck by this new light, is astonished, and shudders and seethes at its own filth, and the work is not carried out without the motion of the Holy Spirit. When they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, Acts 2:37. It is otherwise with infants born in the Church and brought up in its bosom amid the favourable prayers of the saints. Dedicated to God from their tender years, they find that they have been regenerated rather than feel that they have been regenerated, much as we see in natural generation.

units.la: Patet hinc hominem in primo momento novæ hujus generationis se habere mere passive, quando in se spiritualiter mortuus primùm recipit efficaciam Spiritus vivificantis, eiq; inditur principium vitæ spiritualis, ex quo statim agere incipit: ante Regenerationem ergò homo non potest v. g. salutariter audire verbum Dei, totali enim impotentia laborat in ordine ad bona spiritualia salutaria. Hinc Rom. 8. v. 7. Quod sapit caro, inimicitia est adversus Deum: Legi enim Dei non subjicitur, nec potest quidem, 1. Cor. 2. v. 24. Animalis homo non est capax eorum, quæ sunt spiritus Dei; sunt enim ei stultitia, nec potest ea cognoscere, quia spiritualiter dijudicantur.
units.tr: From this it is clear that in the first moment of this new generation man is purely passive, when, spiritually dead in himself, he first receives the efficacy of the vivifying Spirit, and the principle of spiritual life is infused into him, from which he immediately begins to act. Before Regeneration, therefore, a man cannot, for example, hear the Word of God to salvation, for he labours under total inability with respect to spiritual goods that save. Hence Rom. 8:7, The mind of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can it be; 1 Cor. 2:14, The natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; for they are foolishness to him, nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

units.la: Finis subalternus Regenerationis est, quo homo regeneratur in spem vivam, hoc est, hæreditatem, quæ nec perire potest, nec contaminari, nec marcescere, quæ in cœlis servatur: 1. Pet. 1.Pet. 1. v.3. 4. Summus, gloriosæ misericordiæ Dei demonstratio. Rom. 6. v. 4. Ut sicut suscitatus est Christus ad gloriam Dei Patris, ita & nos novâ vitâ ambulemus, nimirum ad gloriam Dei, 1.Cor. 6. v.10. Glorificate Deum in corpore vestro, & in Spiritu vestro, quæ sunt Dei.
units.tr: The subordinate end of Regeneration is that by which a man is regenerated unto a living hope, that is, an inheritance which can neither perish, nor be defiled, nor fade, which is kept in heaven, 1 Pet. 1:3, 4. The highest end is the demonstration of the glorious mercy of God. Rom. 6:4, That as Christ was raised up to the glory of God the Father, so we too should walk in newness of life, namely to the glory of God; 1 Cor. 6:20, Glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's.

units.la: Effecta Regenerationis sunt vires, quas nancisci-mur per eam,quibus tum Deum,tum fratres nostros diligimus, 1. Joh.4.v.7.& 5.v.6. 1.Pet.1.v.22.23. Quibus vincimus mundum, hoc est, quicquid mandatis Dei reluctatur 1. Joh. 5. v.4. Et quibus resistimus peccato, ne illud nobis dominetur, 1.Joh3. v.9. & 5. v. 18.
units.tr: The effects of regeneration are the powers we obtain through it, by which we love both God and our brothers: 1 John 4:7; 5:6; 1 Pet. 1:22-23. By them we overcome the world, that is, whatever resists the commands of God: 1 John 5:4. And by them we resist sin, so that it does not rule over us: 1 John 3:9; 5:18.

units.la: Adjunctorum,quæ sequuntur, Regenerationis primum est tempus, quod variat pro sapientissimo Dei regenerantis consilio & voluntate ; alios enim ante baptismum, alios in baptismo,alios post baptismum; Alios manè,alios, hora tertia, alios sexta, alios nona, quosdam etiam undecima demum hora regenerat, secundum parabolam Matth. 20. v. 1. seqq. Non ergò infantes fœderatorum ante baptismum discedentes hoc beneficio privandi & cœlo excludendi sunt, potest enim Deus ipsis rem Sacramenti conferre absq; Sacramento, licet modus ille, quo hoc fit, nobis non ita sit notus.
units.tr: Of the concomitants that follow, the first is the time of regeneration, which varies according to the most wise counsel and will of God who regenerates. For some he regenerates before baptism, some in baptism, some after baptism; some in the morning, some at the third hour, some at the sixth, some at the ninth, and some at last at the eleventh hour, according to the parable in Matt. 20:1 and following. Therefore the infants of covenant people who die before baptism are not to be deprived of this benefit and shut out of heaven. For God can confer the reality of the sacrament upon them without the sacrament, although the manner in which this is done is not so well known to us.

units.la: Alterum Regenerationis adjunctum est Certitudo, qua quis de sui Regeneratione certus esse potest; fieri potest autem hoc tribus potissimum indiciis. 1. Firmo proposito permanendi in gratia salutari per Christum, Act. 11. v. 17. 18. Hinc Apostoli interrogati, an & ipsi vellent à Christo abire? Respondent; Domine ad quem abibimus? verba vitæ æternæ habes. II. Serio & actuali studio confervandi & confirmandi gratiam Christi, resistendi dubitationibus,cavendi lapsus,& imprimis peccata contra conscientiam. Heb. 6. v.11. 1. Joh.3.v.30. III. Vera & seria resipiscentia post lapsum, qua propositum & studium perseverandi quasi instauratur in fidelibus & renatis. Jerem.31. v.18.19. Pertinet huc Psalm.32. & 51. Patet hinc errare eos, qui absq; speciali & extraordinaria revelatione certitudinem suæ Regenerationis haberi posse negant.
units.tr: The second concomitant of regeneration is certainty, by which a person can be certain of his own regeneration. This can be done chiefly by three signs. (1) A firm purpose of persevering in the saving grace of Christ: Acts 11:17-18. Hence the apostles, when asked whether they also wanted to leave Christ, answer: "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life." (2) Earnest and active zeal for preserving and strengthening the grace of Christ, resisting doubts, guarding against lapses, and above all against sins committed against conscience: Heb. 6:11; 1 John 3:30. (3) True and earnest repentance after a fall, by which the purpose and zeal of persevering is, as it were, renewed in believers and the regenerate: Jer. 31:18-19. To this belong Psalms 32 and 51. It is clear from this that those err who deny that certainty of one's regeneration can be had without a special and extraordinary revelation.

units.la: Tertium: gradus Regenerationis primæ nulli dantur,quia hæc unico momento absolvitur, cùm vita spiritualis partes non admittat, non magis quàm naturalis generatio vel mortuorum vivificatio; Distinguendus enim ab ea est prævius ille apparatus & longa Spiritus molimina, quibus ad conversionem persæpè viam facit: quæ & in mortuorum suscitatione adhibita legimus,2. Reg.4. v.34.36. Quæ moram aliquam plerumq; admittunt, sed in iis formalis Regenerationis ratio non consistit: si verò perfectionem & incrementum spectes, non simul & semel absolvitur, sed per gradus,unde etiam quidam regeniti pueris, quidam verò viris adultis & perfectis comparantur,Hebr.5.& Eph.4. Quemadmodum verò pueri, etsi imperfectius eam exserunt,integram tamen hominis formam, omnibus suis partibus constantem habent, sic neminem verè resipiscentem aut regenitum agnoscimus, nisi qui formam integram ratione partium Regenerationis possidet, etsi quotidie ei sit proficiendum in perfectione graduum.
units.tr: Third: no degrees of the first regeneration are given, because it is accomplished in a single moment, since spiritual life admits no parts, no more than natural generation or the raising of the dead does. For we must distinguish from it that preliminary preparation and the long efforts of the Spirit, by which he often prepares the way for conversion. We read that these were also employed in the raising of the dead: 2 Kings 4:34-36. These often admit some delay, but the formal reason of regeneration does not consist in them. If, however, you look at perfection and growth, it is not completed at once and in a single moment, but by degrees; whence some of the regenerate are compared to children and others to grown and perfect men: Heb. 5 and Eph. 4. But just as children, though they display it more imperfectly, nevertheless have the whole form of a man, consisting of all its parts, so we acknowledge no one as truly repentant or regenerate unless he possesses the whole form with respect to the parts of regeneration, even though he must make daily progress in the perfection of the degrees.

units.la: Quartum; Signa Regenerationis & sanctificationis instauratæq; imaginis Dei in nobis sunt. 1. Fides in Dominum Jesum, 1. Joh.5. v.1. Quisquis credit Jesum esse Christum illum, ex Deo genitus est. II. Charitas erga Deum & proxi-
units.tr: Fourth: the signs of regeneration and sanctification, and of the restored image of God in us, are these. (1) Faith in the Lord Jesus: 1 John 5:1: "Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." (2) Love toward God and neighbour:

units.la: C proximum, 1. Joh. 5. v.1. Et quisquis diligit eum, qui genuit, diligit etiam eum, qui ex eo genitus est. III. Fuga peccatorum & occasionum peccandi, 1. Joh. 5. v. 18. Quisquis natus est ex Deo non peccat: sed qui genitus est ex Deo, conservat seipsum, & malus ille non tangit eum.
units.tr: 1 John 5:1: "And whoever loves him who begot, loves also him who has been begotten by him." (3) Flight from sins and from occasions of sinning: 1 John 5:18: "Whoever is born of God does not sin, but he who was begotten of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him."

units.la: Superest alterum doctrinæ suprà propositæ membrum nempè necessitas Regenerationis quæ inter adjuncta posset esse quintum, & inde probatur, 1. Quia Christus hanc gravissima asseveratione adstruit, Joh.3.v.3. Matt.18.v.3. II. Quia sine ea nemo potest videre regnum Dei & in illud ingredi, Matth. 18. v.3. III. Quia sine ea nemo amicus Dei fieri potest, Rom. 8. v. 7. IV. Quia absq; ea nemo Deo placere potest, Rom. 8. v. 8. Deus enim nobis remittit peccata, ut in posterum desinamus eum offendere peccatis nostris. Non possumus autem à peccatis desistere, nisi natura nostra per Spiritum Sanctum instauretur: Sed manum de tabula; ipse Deus pacis sanctificet nos totos: & integer noster spiritus, & anima & corpus inculpatè, in adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi conservemur; fidelis est; qui vocavit nos, qui etiam id efficiet, cui sit laus in secula A M E N!
units.tr: There remains the other member of the doctrine proposed above, namely the necessity of regeneration, which could be counted as the fifth concomitant. It is proved thus: (1) because Christ asserts it with the gravest solemnity: John 3:3; Matt. 18:3. (2) Because without it no one can see the kingdom of God or enter into it: Matt. 18:3. (3) Because without it no one can become a friend of God: Rom. 8:7. (4) Because without it no one can please God: Rom. 8:8. For God forgives us our sins so that in future we may cease to offend him by our sins. But we cannot desist from sins unless our nature is restored through the Holy Spirit. But enough of this. May the God of peace himself sanctify us wholly, and may our whole spirit, soul and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Faithful is he who called us, who also will do it, to whom be praise for ever and ever. AMEN!
To the most distinguished author, my most excellent fellow student.

units.la: Numquid JACOBE ludimur, Fortunæ volucri ludimur impetu! Æternum nihil est sacro Quicquid lenta tulit materies sinu. Statur casibus. Occidet Quod surgit, sed adhuc surget & occidet, Ritu præcipitis pilæ, Quæ cum pulsa cava rejicitur manu, Nunc leves secat Africos, Nunc terræ refugis absilit ictibus: Vesper vespere truditur, Sed nunc deterior, nunc melior subit: Magnas Fors rapit interim Urbesq; & populos & miserabili Reges subruit impetu: Et sceptri decus, & regna cadentium Permiscet cineri Ducum; Auratasq; trabes & penetralia Et cives simul & super Eversis sepelit turribus oppida. Sic quod prodit in Orbem Jam jam magnificè, cras miserè perit; Florens hic hodie occidit, Surgit mox alius natus ad aspera. Eheu JACOBE ludimur, Fatorum rapidâ ludimur orbitâ!
units.tr: Are we being toyed with, Jacob? We are toyed with by the winged rush of Fortune! Nothing is eternal that slow matter has ever borne in its sacred bosom. Things stand only by chance. What rises falls, yet it will rise again and fall again, like a falling ball that, struck by the hollow hand, is flung back: now it cuts through the light southwest winds, now it leaps from the earth with repeated blows. Evening is thrust forward by evening; now a worse thing comes on, now a better. Meanwhile Fortune seizes great cities and peoples, and with pitiable force overthrows kings, and mingles the glory of the sceptre and the realms of fallen leaders with their ashes. She buries gilded beams and inner chambers, citizens and towns together under towers thrown down. So what comes forth into the world now splendidly, tomorrow perishes wretchedly. The flourishing man falls today; soon another, born for hardship, rises. Alas, Jacob, we are toyed with by the swift orbit of the fates!

units.la: Quid! nil perpetuum cedò, Quicquid tellus habet singula lubrica? Est, semper quod, ais, manet, Est quid, quod faciem non variat suam; Est, quæ permanet, altera Constans ac stabilis, vera, creatio, Quâ Sol Justitiæ Sacer Vult signare suos, quos amat ac fovet, Per Flamen radians suum, Mortem ne videant insuper horridam, Quos divellere non queunt A' Christo Domino nec bona nec mala. Hæc non vertit imaginem, Quæ cras,est hodie, cuncta ruant licet, Nunquàm non eadem stat hæc; Fiet terra polus, nix prius atra erit, Ante agnus comedet lupum, Ullis viribus hæc quàm detur irrita. Hem! quis doctus hic HALLER est? Dignus qui reliquas exeat ad Scholas.
units.tr: What! Tell me, is nothing perpetual, since everything the earth holds is slippery? You say there is something that always remains; there is something that does not change its face. There is another creation that abides, constant, stable and true, by which the holy Sun of Righteousness wishes to mark his own, whom he loves and cherishes, shining through his own Spirit, so that they may not see dreadful death beyond; neither good nor evil can tear them from Christ the Lord. This creation does not alter its image: what is today will be the same tomorrow, though all things fall. It never ceases to stand the same. The earth will become the sky, snow will turn black first, the lamb will eat the wolf before this creation is made void by any powers. Hem! Who is this learned Haller? He is worthy to go forth to the remaining schools.

units.la: Hoc amicitiæ non intermoritura πυμήνειον[?] annectere voluit, cujus
